prod_006:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare to create our code hosting organization on {{vendor}} (our canonical code hosting platform). Please do the preparatory work only — do not submit the organization creation form or accept any terms yourself.

First, ask me for any missing inputs you need:
- Desired organization name/slug (and 1-2 backup names in case of conflicts)
- The primary contact email and the account that should be the org owner
- Our company/domain name (for verification and branding)
- Expected team names and their initial members (for later repo/team access planning)
- Any known naming conventions or existing repos to migrate

Then prepare the following as drafts, ready for me to review:
1. A filled-out summary of all values needed for the {{vendor}} organization creation form (org name, owner account, contact email, plan tier if relevant).
2. A checklist of the org-level settings we'll want to configure after creation, based on best practices: granular access permissions at workspace/project/repo/branch level, branch protection and merge-check policies, and baseline CI/CD policy enforcement expectations.
3. A short summary of what the organization owner is agreeing to (billing responsibility and terms of service acceptance) so I understand what I'm approving — describe this in plain language, do not quote any specific legal text.
4. A proposed initial repo and team structure based on the team names I gave you.

Once this package is ready, present it to me clearly labeled (org details, settings checklist, terms/billing summary, repo/team plan) and then stop for human sign-off. Do not create the organization, accept the terms of service, commit to any billing plan, or submit the form — that step requires me, as the authenticated account owner, to complete manually. Report back with the full prepared package and a note confirming you stopped before submission.

prod_006:n2.prompt:
You are helping me create repositories in our {{vendor}} code hosting organization as part of setting up our code hosting org. This step requires my explicit approval before any changes are applied, so you must prepare everything but not execute repository creation until I confirm.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already known:
- The name of our {{vendor}} organization
- The list of repositories to create (name, visibility — private/public/internal, and a short description for each)
- Whether each repo should be initialized with a README, .gitignore template, and/or license file
- Any naming convention or default branch name I want used (e.g. main)

Once I provide these, use your configured credentials to check the {{vendor}} organization for existing repositories with the same names to avoid collisions, and prepare a clear plan listing each repository to be created along with its visibility, description, initialization options, and default branch. Present this plan to me as a checklist for review.

Do not create any repositories yet. This step requires a human to explicitly approve before changes are applied, so after presenting the plan, stop for human sign-off.

Once I approve, create the repositories exactly as specified via the {{vendor}} dashboard or API, using words to describe each operation (e.g., "create a new private repository named X with a README") rather than any raw endpoint syntax. After creation, verify each repository exists, is reachable, and has the correct visibility and default branch, then report back a summary table showing each repository's name, visibility, default branch, and a link to its location, plus any errors or repos that already existed and were skipped.

prod_006:n3.prompt:
You are helping me configure branch protection rules for our {{vendor}} code hosting organization, as part of setting up our repos and team access. Before starting, ask me for: (1) the organization name on {{vendor}}, (2) the list of repositories that need protection rules, (3) the branch(es) to protect in each (typically main/master and any release branches), and (4) our intended policy — e.g., require pull request reviews before merging (and how many approvals), require status checks/CI to pass, restrict who can push directly, require linear history, and whether to block force pushes and branch deletion.

Using your configured credentials, access {{vendor}} and, for each specified repository, prepare (but do not yet apply) a draft branch protection configuration covering: required reviewers/approval counts, required status checks, restrictions on direct pushes, force-push and deletion protection, and any granular access rules for the branch consistent with our stated policy. Summarize each proposed rule set clearly per repository so I can review it.

Because this change requires explicit human approval before being applied, do not save, enable, or apply any branch protection settings yet. Compile a clear checklist/summary of the proposed rules for every repository and branch, present it to me, and then stop for human sign-off.

Once I review and approve, let me know you're ready to proceed, but do not apply anything until I give explicit confirmation. In your final report, list: the organization name, each repository and branch covered, the full proposed protection settings per branch, and confirmation that no changes have been applied pending my approval.

prod_006:n4.prompt:
You are helping me set up teams and access control in our {{vendor}} code hosting organization. Please use your configured credentials to interact with {{vendor}} on my behalf.

First, ask me for: (1) the organization name/URL on {{vendor}}, (2) the list of teams I want created (e.g., names like 'backend', 'frontend', 'devops', 'contractors'), (3) for each team, which members should belong to it, and (4) for each team, which repositories it needs access to and at what permission level (e.g., read, write, admin, or maintain).

Once I provide this, do the following:
1. Draft a clear plan mapping each team to its members and to its repo access levels, using the granular permission model {{vendor}} supports at the workspace, project, repository, and branch level.
2. Check the current state of the organization (existing teams, members, repos) via the dashboard or API to avoid duplicates or conflicts.
3. Prepare the exact set of actions needed: which teams to create, which members to add to each, and which repo permissions to assign to each team — written out plainly, not executed yet.
4. Flag any ambiguities (e.g., a team with no members listed, or a repo not yet created) and ask me to resolve them before proceeding.

Because a human must explicitly approve before changes are applied, do NOT create teams or set permissions yet. Present the full plan as a checklist for my review and then stop for human sign-off.

When reporting back, give me: the proposed team list with members, the proposed repo access matrix, and any open questions or conflicts you found, so I can approve or adjust before you apply anything.

prod_006:n5.prompt:
You are helping me invite team members to our {{vendor}} code hosting organization as part of setting up our org structure. Before starting, ask me for: (1) the org/workspace name on {{vendor}}, (2) the list of team members to invite (name, email or {{vendor}} username, and intended role/permission level for each — e.g. owner, maintainer, write, read), and (3) any team groupings or repository-specific access rules I want applied (e.g. certain repos or branches restricted to specific people).

Once you have this information, use my configured credentials to access {{vendor}} and prepare the invitations: draft the list of members to be invited along with their proposed role and access scope (org-level, team-level, repository-level, or branch-level as applicable), consistent with granular permission controls. If {{vendor}} supports teams/groups, propose a team structure that matches the access rules I gave you. Do not send the invitations or apply any permission changes yet.

Because approval is required before changes are applied, compile everything into a clear summary: who is being invited, their role, and their access scope, plus any team structure you're proposing. Present this summary to me and then stop for human sign-off — do not click invite, send invitations, or submit any changes until I explicitly approve.

When you report back, include: the full list of proposed invitees with roles and access levels, any team/group structure recommended, and a note confirming that no invitations have been sent and no permissions have been changed, pending my approval.
